human_answer.name: Pierce A. & Rusheel N.
human_answer.reasoning: Cutting 2029 government growth from 22% to 12% makes 2029 government revenue about 8% smaller. Margins are fixed, so operating profit and free cash flow fall too. The smaller 2029 base carries into 2030 and the terminal value, so value per diluted share falls. The drop should be modest, about 3–4%, because only one year and roughly half of revenue change.
human_answer.decision: The do-not-initiate action stays the same, and the case for it gets slightly stronger. Intrinsic value is already well below $189.40, so a lower value only widens that gap. The change can’t push value above the threshold, so the decision holds.

units: fraction of prior-year government revenue; 22% to 12%
held_fixed: All other growth inputs, operating margins, tax, WACC, working capital, capex, terminal convention, valuation date, share basis and reference price
